Traditional Panettone

Served at: New Year's Day · Fourth Sunday of Advent

One 2 lb (900g) PanettonePrep 1 hour 30 min active (plus 10-14 hours passive rising)Cook 45-55 min

Panettone is a classic Italian sweet bread, rich with eggs, butter, and candied fruits. It's a beloved symbol of Christmas, often enjoyed throughout the Advent season, particularly on the Fourth Sunday, and continues to be a festive treat well into the New Year, gracing tables on New Year's Day as a symbol of good fortune and celebration.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (160g) golden raisins
  • 1/2 cup (80g) diced candied orange peel
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) dark rum or brandy
  • For the Preferment:
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) warm whole milk (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 1 teaspoon (3g) active dry yeast
  • 1 teaspoon (4g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (60g) bread flour
  • For the Main Dough:
  • 3 1/2 cups (420g) bread flour, divided
  • 3/4 cup (150g) granulated sugar, divided
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast
  • 3 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 3 large egg yolks, at room temperature
  • 1 teaspoon (6g) fine sea salt
  • 1 tablespoon (5ml) vanilla extract
  • 1 tablespoon (5g) orange zest (from 1 large orange)
  • 1 teaspoon (2g) lemon zest (from 1 small lemon)
  • 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter, very soft, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) pieces
  • 1 Panettone paper mold, 7-inch (18 cm) diameter x 4.5-inch (11 cm) tall

Method

  1. Prepare the fruits: In a small bowl, combine the golden raisins, candied orange peel, and rum or brandy. Let soak for at least 30 minutes, or preferably overnight, stirring occasionally. Drain well and pat dry before adding to the dough.
  2. Make the preferment: In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the warm milk, 1 teaspoon yeast, 1 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 cup (60g) bread flour. Whisk until smooth. Cover with plastic wrap and let sit in a warm place for 30-60 minutes, until bubbly and foamy.
  3. First Dough: To the preferment, add 1 cup (120g) of the remaining bread flour, 1/4 cup (50g) of the remaining granulated sugar, 1 whole egg, and 1 egg yolk. Attach the dough hook to your stand mixer and mix on low speed for 2 minutes, then increase to medium-low and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
  4. Transfer the dough to a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 2-3 hours, or until doubled in size.
  5. Second Dough: Return the first dough to the stand mixer bowl. Add the remaining 2 1/2 cups (300g) bread flour, remaining 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar, remaining 1 1/4 teaspoons (4g) yeast, remaining 2 whole eggs, remaining 2 egg yolks, salt, vanilla extract, orange zest, and lemon zest. Mix on low speed for 5 minutes until combined, then increase to medium-low and knead for 10-15 minutes until the dough is very elastic and pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
  6. With the mixer running on medium-low, add the softened butter, one piece at a time, allowing each piece to be fully incorporated before adding the next. This process will take 10-15 minutes. Continue kneading until the dough is very smooth, shiny, and passes the 'windowpane test' (you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
  7. Add the drained, dried fruits to the dough and mix on low speed for 1-2 minutes until evenly distributed.
  8. Transfer the dough to a large, lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 2-3 hours, or until nearly doubled in size.
  9. Gently deflate the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Shape it into a tight ball. Place the dough into the panettone paper mold.
  10. Cover the mold loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it proof in a warm place for 3-5 hours, or until the dough has risen to the top edge of the mold and is visibly puffy.
  11. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). If desired, use a sharp knife or razor blade to cut a shallow 'X' on top of the panettone and place a small pat of butter in the center.
  12. Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a thermometer inserted into the center reads 195-200°F (90-93°C). If the top browns too quickly, loosely tent with foil.
  13. Immediately upon removing from the oven, insert two long metal skewers horizontally through the base of the panettone, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) from the bottom, parallel to each other. Invert the panettone and hang it upside down (e.g., between two chairs or over a pot) for at least 4-6 hours, or overnight, to cool completely. This prevents the rich, airy crumb from collapsing.
  14. Once completely cool, remove the skewers. Panettone is best enjoyed sliced and served at room temperature.

Tips

  • A stand mixer with a dough hook is highly recommended for this recipe, as the dough is very rich and sticky.
  • Do not rush the rising times; proper fermentation is crucial for Panettone's characteristic flavor and texture. A slightly cooler rise (e.g., in the refrigerator overnight for the bulk fermentation) can further develop flavor.
  • Cooling the Panettone upside down is essential to maintain its tall, airy structure and prevent it from compacting under its own weight.
